props.title: TruthOps — ==verification you can== **audit**.
props.subtitle: Transparent, rule-based misinformation verification with photo forensics — and a human approval gate before anything ships.

slides.notes: Open with the promise: no black boxes. Every verdict is explainable, every run is auditable, and a human signs off before a response plan goes out.

left.label: Speed
left.title: Claims outrun fact-checks
points: Viral claims spread in hours; fact-checks take days
Manual review can't scale to the volume

right.label: Trust
right.title: Black-box AI isn't believed
points: "The model said so" convinces no one
No evidence chain means no accountability

slides.notes: Two failures compounding: fact-checking is too slow for viral spread, and opaque AI verdicts get dismissed even when they're right. TruthOps attacks both.

tiles.title: Score high-risk claims
tiles.body: Flags the claims most likely to cause harm before any deep analysis runs.

tiles.title: Photo forensics
tiles.body: Runs image analysis to surface manipulated or miscaptioned photos.

tiles.title: Scripted contrarian check
tiles.body: A deterministic pass that argues the other side — no vibes, just rules.

tiles.title: Gather evidence
tiles.body: Pulls primary sources via Firecrawl and the Alexandria corpus.

tiles.title: Evidence-backed response plans
tiles.body: Outputs a plan a human can approve, amend, or reject — with receipts.

slides.notes: Walk the five capabilities briefly. Emphasize that the contrarian pass is scripted and rule-based — the system argues against its own verdict on purpose.

items.title: Intake
items.body: Claims and media enter the queue

slides.notes: Trace the flow end to end. Land hard on the last step: the human approval gate is a hard stop, not a suggestion.

props.title: Every verdict ships its ==audit trail==.
props.code:
{
  "claim": "Viral post claims X",
  "verdict": "unsupported",
  "confidence": 0.86,
  "evidence_chain": [
    "source: firecrawl/snapshot-412",
    "source: alexandria/entry-8829",
    "forensics: photo/exif-mismatch"
  ],
  "contrarian_pass": "passed",
  "human_approval": "pending",
  "cost_usd": 0.0427,
  "observability": "neatlogs/run-7f3a"
}

slides.notes: The point of this slide: nothing is hidden. neatlogs observability records every run, and the economics of each verification are costed to the cent — reproducible and reviewable.

items.title: Rules over vibes
items.body: Deterministic, scriptable checks — the same input always yields the same audit.

items.title: Photo forensics built in
items.body: Manipulated and miscaptioned images get analyzed, not just the text.

items.title: Human approval gate
items.body: AI drafts, evidence supports, a person decides. No autonomous verdicts.

items.title: Costed to the cent
items.body: Every run's economics are logged — transparency extends to the bill.

slides.notes: Pick two of the four to dwell on based on the room — the approval gate for policy folks, cent-level costing for engineers.
Status beat: this isn't a mockup. It was built for neatHack 2026, submitted October 12, and the repo is public and running.
